output.diagnosis: Habitually slow but ultimately full-paying payer: six prior invoices all settled PAID_FULL, each between roughly two weeks and six weeks past due. This invoice is 27 days past its due date, still fully outstanding, no contacts have been made yet and no payment link has been sent. Payer notes record only a vague verbal commitment from the accounts officer that the transfer goes out 'once the season picks up', with an internal observation that prior dated commitments were honoured only once. There is no dispute description, no email reply, no documentation request, and no hardship language in the record.

drafted_message.body:
Dear Mr. Gurpreet Singh Bedi,

We are writing regarding invoice ASH-2026-0024, which remains open on our records past its due date.

We understand from your accounts officer that the transfer is expected once the season picks up. If you can share when the payment is likely to be released, we will note it against the account and hold off on further follow-ups in the meantime.

If any statement or supporting document would help you process this, please let us know and we will send it across.

Thank you for your continued business.

Regards,
Accounts Receivable Team
drafted_message.subject: Invoice ASH-2026-0024 - payment status

output.reasoning: No commercial objection, missing-document blocker, already-paid claim, or distress signal is visible, so this reads as ordinary late payment within this payer's established pattern rather than something needing human judgement. Because no contact has been attempted at all and the only commitment on file is open-ended ('once the season picks up') rather than a specific cycle or dated promise, WAIT would leave the account drifting without any first touch. A single low-pressure service reminder is the proportionate opening step; escalation or a link push is not yet justified given the clean full-payment history. Uncertainty: the verbal commitment may reflect genuine seasonal cash timing that a reminder cannot accelerate, and the note that earlier commitments were honoured only once is a soft internal impression, not evidence of intent.
